We used 30 predefined Butina-cluster-disjoint train/validation/test splits (Morgan radius 2, 2,048 bits, achiral fingerprints; Tanimoto-distance cutoff 0.35). To quantify residual structural proximity not captured by cluster membership, we identified the nearest reference analogue for every validation and test molecule using maximum Tanimoto similarity (Supplementary Table S4). Across the 30 splits, the test-to-train median nearest-neighbour similarity was 0.537 $\pm$ 0.003; the P95 was 0.740 $\pm$ 0.008. The fraction of test molecules with a nearest training analogue of at least 0.80 was 2.517 $\pm$ 0.370\%, and that at least 0.90 was 0.251 $\pm$ 0.144\%. Thus, cluster-disjoint splitting removed shared cluster membership but did not create a strictly out-of-domain test set; residual close analogues are reported as a limitation rather than removed by post hoc split tuning.
